recommended_model.rationale: The nutriments table serves as the fact table because it contains quantitative measurements related to products, which can be analyzed in conjunction with product details, categories, and ingredients.

quality_findings: Inconsistent casing/format detected in product_name column of products table.
Inconsistent casing/format detected in brands column of products table.
Inconsistent casing/format detected in ingredient_id column of ingredients table.
Inconsistent casing/format detected in ingredient_text column of ingredients table.
Inconsistent casing/format detected in category_tag column of categories table.
data_science_opportunities: Churn prediction could be implemented by analyzing customer purchasing patterns and product preferences.
Demand forecasting can be enhanced by analyzing historical sales data and seasonal trends in product categories.
Nutritional analysis and recommendation systems could be developed to suggest healthier alternatives based on ingredient composition.

kpis.name: Average Nutrient Value by Product Category
kpis.sql: SELECT c.category_tag, AVG(CAST(n.value AS REAL)) AS avg_nutrient_value FROM nutriments n JOIN categories c ON n.product_code = c.product_code GROUP BY c.category_tag ORDER BY avg_nutrient_value DESC LIMIT 10;
kpis.why_it_matters: Understanding the average nutrient value by category helps in assessing the healthiness of product offerings.

kpis.name: Total Products by Brand
kpis.sql: SELECT p.brands, COUNT(*) AS total_products FROM products p GROUP BY p.brands ORDER BY total_products DESC LIMIT 10;
kpis.why_it_matters: This KPI provides insight into brand performance and market presence.

kpis.name: Total Ingredients by Product
kpis.sql: SELECT i.product_code, COUNT(*) AS total_ingredients FROM ingredients i GROUP BY i.product_code ORDER BY total_ingredients DESC LIMIT 10;
kpis.why_it_matters: Identifying products with the most ingredients can help in understanding complexity and potential allergen risks.

kpis.name: Vegan Product Count by Category
kpis.sql: SELECT c.category_tag, COUNT(*) AS vegan_product_count FROM products p JOIN categories c ON p.code = c.product_code WHERE p.code IN (SELECT product_code FROM ingredients WHERE vegan = 'yes') GROUP BY c.category_tag ORDER BY vegan_product_count DESC LIMIT 10;
kpis.why_it_matters: This KPI highlights the availability of vegan options across different categories, catering to a growing consumer segment.

kpis.name: Average Percent Estimate of Ingredients by Product
kpis.sql: SELECT i.product_code, AVG(CAST(i.percent_estimate AS REAL)) AS avg_percent_estimate FROM ingredients i GROUP BY i.product_code ORDER BY avg_percent_estimate DESC LIMIT 10;
kpis.why_it_matters: This metric helps in assessing the primary ingredients in products and their estimated proportions.

insights: The average nutrient value for pink Himalayan salt and Himalayan salts is significantly high at approximately 1233, indicating that these products are nutrient-rich. This could be a strong selling point for health-conscious consumers.

Kroger leads the market with 1,645 products, followed by Roundy's and Spartan. This dominance suggests that Kroger has a robust market presence, which could be leveraged in marketing strategies to attract more customers.

There are 11,933 vegan products categorized as 'undefined', which indicates a potential data quality issue. This inconsistency may mislead consumers looking for vegan options, affecting their trust in the brand.

The highest number of ingredients in a product is 79, which may raise concerns about complexity and allergen risks for consumers. Simplifying ingredient lists could enhance product appeal and consumer trust.

The average percent estimate of ingredients shows some products exceeding 100%, which is unrealistic and indicates a data quality issue. This could undermine confidence in product labeling and should be addressed to maintain brand integrity.
